research_concepts: defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 scoring change
regression to the mean in H1->H2 change
methodological_questions: Is the between-team variance of opponent H2-H1 change larger than sampling noise (split-half and cross-season reliability)?
Does the effect persist after conditioning on the opponent's H1 level (RTM), opponent baseline H2-H1 tendency, game state, and overall defensive quality?
Is the observed reliability above a placebo (shuffled team labels) and mechanical floor?
Is 120 team-seasons enough to detect a plausible reliability?

historical_evidence.finding: Variance of H1->H2 PPP collapse: H1 PPP alone (RTM) explains 32.9% of variance. Usage, process/shot-zone, lineup and context add about 0 to 1.7 pp. 65.4% is unexplained and is described as idiosyncratic noise from small per-half n (n=40963 cells, 12617 triggers). Recorded as a powered null (B_powered_null).

The A1 adaptation falsification found no carryover: next-game PPP Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842. The adapter-minus-no-signal gap was negative and grew with vote confidence, so the adapter PPP lift looked like a construction, selection or label artifact. Limitations recorded: label error and selection/RTM.

Defensive scheme change within and across games used inferred labels. Change was found in 99% of units, and transition matrices were near-uniform. The record says inferred labels cannot separate real defensive adjustment from the offense executing differently.
Descriptive only: team AVOID% in H2 trigger games ranged from 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC) across 55 series, with no outcome test. Player samples were 10-178 possessions.
Series-level AVOID share vs winning gave rho=-0.26, p=0.07 at n=50 series (verdict inconclusive). The record is confounded by team quality and says about 80 series are needed.
The player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap was +0.427 at n>=10 per tier. Only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers. This is a different question (counter choice, not defense reliability).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Explaining H1->H2 PPP collapse with process, usage, lineup and context features
failed_approaches.why: RTM accounts for about 95% of the explained variance. The residual is noise from small per-half samples.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating the adapter PPP lift as a real coverage response
failed_approaches.why: Selection/RTM and label error. There was no carryover to the next game and no confidence dose-response in the expected direction.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme change from inferred play-type labels
failed_approaches.why: Label noise cannot be separated from offensive execution differences.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level test of a team tendency against outcome
failed_approaches.why: Too few units (n=50) and a team-quality confound.

evidence_establishes: Per-half PPP differences are dominated by regression to the mean and noise in this project's records (FAM:SF-APPS-076, recorded as rejected). Observable process, lineup and context features added almost nothing.
Team differences in counter-choice shares (AVOID%) exist descriptively (FAM:SF-APPS-015), but nothing records whether they persist or are caused by the defense.
Inferred play-type and scheme labels have documented reliability problems (FAM:SF-APPA-001, FAM:SF-APPA-005, FAM:SF-APPA-030 as artifact/inconclusive).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record directly tests team-level reliability (split-half or cross-season) of the opponent H2-H1 change.
The prior null was at the trigger/possession-cell level, not the team-season level. It does not say whether a small stable team component exists.
Whether any team-level effect would survive opponent adjustment and game-state controls is not recorded.
own_inferences: With about 40 games per half-sample and a large per-game SD of H2-H1 margin, sampling noise probably swamps any true team SD of under about 1 point per 100 possessions, so reliability is probably low.
If reliability is estimated without removing the H1-level RTM component, it may look positive because of a mechanical link to team defensive quality or pace. That would be an artifact.
Team defense of opponents' H2-H1 change is confounded with the team's own offense, starter minutes and blowout rates. Garbage-time filtering must be applied symmetrically to avoid selection.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'defense's effect' is not given. It could be PPP, points or efficiency, and raw or opponent-adjusted.
Whether playoffs are pooled with the regular season. Playoff samples per team-season are small, and opponents are repeated.
Whether the 120 units include 4 seasons x 30 teams. Cross-season pairs number at most 90 and are not independent.
No prior record gives the empirical per-game SD of H2-H1 change or a plausible true team SD.

historical_effect.explanation: The RTM-dominated powered null in FAM:SF-APPS-076 and the artifact findings in FAM:SF-APPA-001 moved the decision from a plain 'proceed' to 'proceed_with_changes'. The change adds an explicit RTM/opponent adjustment, a placebo and noise-floor comparison, and reliability reporting with a confidence interval, with a low prior that a reliable trait exists. The history also supports avoiding inferred scheme labels.

blocking_constraints.text: With 120 team-seasons, a cross-season test has at most 90 non-independent pairs. It can detect only r of about 0.3 or more at 80% power, and a smaller true reliability would be indistinguishable from zero.
The per-game H2-H1 difference is very noisy, so split-half reliability may be bounded near zero by noise even if a real trait exists.

prior_work.summary: The retrieved records give a powered null on explaining trigger-level H1->H2 collapse beyond RTM and artifact/untestable results on adaptation and scheme labels. None directly measures the team-level reliability of defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change.

risks.text: Opponent H2-H1 change is mechanically negatively correlated with H1 level. The H1 level and the opponent's baseline must be modelled out, otherwise reliability is mechanical.
Garbage time, blowouts, starter rest, pace, the team's own offense, opponent quality and schedule, and overall defensive quality all drive H2-H1 change.
Per-half possession counts are small, so the team-level signal-to-noise ratio is low. Reliability must be reported with a CI and a noise-ceiling comparison.
There are only 120 team-seasons, and cross-season pairs are not independent. Playoffs add few games per team.
Rosters, coaches and rules change across the four seasons, so persistence across seasons understates a within-season trait.
The result is interpretable only relative to shuffled-team or random-split nulls that preserve game-state structure.
Multiple definitions (PPP, margin, filters) and subsets could inflate false positives unless fixed in advance.
The design must avoid inferred play-type or scheme labels, which the project's records show to be unreliable.

design.estimand: Reliability (ICC and odd/even-game split-half correlation, Spearman-Brown corrected, plus year-to-year correlation) of each defense's team-specific effect on opponents' H2-H1 PPP change. The effect is the residual after regressing the opponent's H2-H1 change on opponent H1 PPP, the opponent's season baseline H2-H1 tendency, pace, home/away and rest. It is reported as the team random effect SD.
design.unit: Team-season (defense), built from game-level opponent H1 and H2 possession-level PPP. Mixed model: game within defense-season, with opponent random effects.
design.sample: All 30 teams x 4 seasons (2022-23 to 2025-26) = 120 team-seasons, regular season only for the primary analysis. Playoffs are a secondary analysis, not pooled. Exclude games with a margin over 25 at any H2 point, applied symmetrically, with a sensitivity run without the exclusion. Use complete 2025-26 data only.
design.power: Within-season split-half uses about 40 games per half, with r detectable at about 0.25 on n=120. Cross-season has at most 90 pairs and detects r of about 0.30 at 80% power. A simulation using the empirical per-game SD should be run before analysis to give the noise ceiling and a minimum detectable team SD. If the ceiling is under 0.2, report the question as underpowered.
design.controls: Opponent H1 PPP (RTM), opponent baseline H2-H1, opponent strength, home/away, rest, garbage-time exclusion, pace and defense's overall rating (to separate it from general defensive quality). No inferred play-type or scheme labels.
design.falsification: Placebo A: permute defense labels within opponent and month to give a null reliability distribution (1000 permutations). Placebo B: random game splits, which should give reliability equal to the noise-only value. Control: confirm that reliability of the raw (unadjusted) H2-H1 change is not larger than the adjusted one for mechanical reasons. A reliable trait requires adjusted reliability above the permutation 95th percentile and a team SD whose CI excludes 0.
design.multiplicity: One primary estimand (PPP, regular season, split-half and cross-season). Secondary analyses (playoffs, margin, no-exclusion) are labelled exploratory with Holm correction across them.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the adjusted split-half (corrected) r is 0.3 or more with the lower 95% CI bound above the permutation null AND the cross-season r has a CI excluding 0. Rejected if the CI upper bound on reliability is under 0.2 with a noise-ceiling check showing adequate power. Otherwise report as inconclusive/underpowered. Do not describe any positive result as a causal defensive effect without the controls.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, rotation and box-score files for 2022-23 through 2025-26. 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13 and playoffs from 2026-06-21. Freeze the data snapshot and code hash at pre-registration on 2026-10-06.

between-season persistence of team defensive effect
methodological_questions: Is a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change stable across seasons (split-half or year-to-year reliability)?
How much of the team-level variance in H2-H1 change is signal versus noise given 120 team-seasons?
How should regression to the mean, game-state/garbage-time selection, and opponent strength be handled?
Is the effect distinguishable from a placebo or mechanical floor and from overall defensive quality?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to call a follow-up tool, but I think I can finish from what I have. The key evidence is that the RTM variable explains about 32.9% of the H1-to-H2 PPP collapse, the process adds only about 1.7 points, and the rest looks like noise, so FAM:SF-APPS-076 gets rejected. I'm also checking the other families: FAM:SF-APPA-001 looks like an artifact of the adaptation tests, and FAM:SF-APPA-005 can't be tested because its labels are inferred.

I'm setting up the design for a reliability check: how consistent each team's defense is in how much the opponent's scoring changes from the first half to the second half, adjusted for the opponent's first-half level. That covers 120 team-seasons across 30 teams, so I'm weighing year-to-year pairs and odd-even game splits, expecting low reliability given the noisy per-game differences.

I'm settling on how to define the defense effect: the change in an opponent's second-half minus first-half scoring, measured against that opponent's usual pattern so regression to the mean and garbage-time effects are accounted for. The predicted outcome is mostly rejection or an uncertain result, with roughly a 60% chance the test is workable, so I'm leaning toward proceeding with some changes.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to call a follow-up tool, but I think I can finish from what I have. The key evidence is that the RTM variable explains about 32.9% of the H1-to-H2 PPP collapse, the process adds only about 1.7 points, and the rest looks like noise, so FAM:SF-APPS-076 gets rejected. I'm also checking the other families: FAM:SF-APPA-001 looks like an artifact of the adaptation tests, and FAM:SF-APPA-005 can't be tested because its labels are inferred.

I'm setting up the design for a reliability check: how consistent each team's defense is in how much the opponent's scoring changes from the first half to the second half, adjusted for the opponent's first-half level. That covers 120 team-seasons across 30 teams, so I'm weighing year-to-year pairs and odd-even game splits, expecting low reliability given the noisy per-game differences.

I'm settling on how to define the defense effect: the change in an opponent's second-half minus first-half scoring, measured against that opponent's usual pattern so regression to the mean and garbage-time effects are accounted for. The predicted outcome is mostly rejection or an uncertain result, with roughly a 60% chance the test is workable, so I'm leaning toward proceeding with some changes.
